No logs yet.\n\nTurn on what to record above, then play a game: its logs appear here.

E-mail addresses, tokens and keys are removed as logs are written. File paths are kept so the logs stay useful — glance over them before sharing if a folder name identifies you. Logcat holds this app\'s output only.
That folder can\'t be written to. Pick another one.
Delete %1$s of logs of %2$s?\n\nOnly files WinlatorMali wrote are removed.

One switch for all logging.

Off, nothing at all is recorded: no Wine or Box64 / FEXCore output, no DXVK or VKD3D logs (they are kept silent), no logcat, no crash reports and no exit reasons, and no folders are created. Your choices below are kept and come back when you turn it on again.

Logs already on disk stay listed here, so you can still read, share or delete them.

No performance cost.

Gives each game its own folder inside your log location, named after the shortcut (or the container, when you start one without a shortcut), so one game's logs don't get mixed up with another's. Each folder keeps the last runs under "previous".

Turn it off to keep everything in one folder; past runs are then not kept. Logs already written are left where they are.

⚠️ SLOWS GAMES DOWN. Only turn this on to diagnose a problem, then turn it back off.

Records what Wine itself is doing, as wine_debug.log in the game's folder. Every message is written as the game runs, and Wine produces a lot of them — the "seh" channel alone logs an entry every time the game raises an exception. Heavier channels such as "relay" can make a game many times slower.

This is the log to enable when a game won't start, crashes, or dies at launch. The channels below choose what Wine reports.

⚠️ SLOWS GAMES DOWN at higher verbosity.

Records what the x86 translator (Box64 for x86_64 Wine, FEXCore or WOWBox64 for arm64ec) is doing while it runs the game's PC code, into the same wine_debug.log. Useful for a game that crashes in a way Wine's own log doesn't explain, or misbehaves under only one translator.

Leave off for normal play.

Little to no performance cost.

Records what the graphics layers report — DXVK for DirectX 8/9/10/11 (<game>_d3d11.log, <game>_dxgi.log…), VKD3D for DirectX 12 (vkd3d-proton.log). Almost everything is written while the game starts: which GPU and driver were picked, which features are missing, why a shader failed.

The log to check for black screens, missing textures or a refused graphics feature. Safe to leave on. Off, DXVK and VKD3D are kept silent.

No performance cost.

Android's own log, as it relates to WinlatorMali: the renderer, the X server, input and audio. It is saved once, when a game exits (logcat.log in its folder), or when you tap "Capture logcat" — never continuously, so it costs no frames.

It contains THIS APP'S OUTPUT ONLY: Android doesn't let an app read other apps' logs, and nothing system-wide is captured, so other apps' data never ends up in a file you share.
No performance cost.\n\nIf the app itself crashes, the error and the moments before it are saved as crash_<time>.txt in the app logs, before Android closes it. Send that file when you report a crash.

No performance cost.\n\nAndroid keeps a short record of why the app\'s last processes ended: a crash, a native crash, \"not responding\", killed for low memory, or closed normally. With this on, a new record is saved to the app logs each time the app starts — useful when a game closes with no error at all, which is usually Android killing it for memory. \"Exit reasons\" below shows the records any time.
